significance: A tenth-century goddess shrine on the 1,575-foot Kolhua hill in Chatra district, revered as a Shakta pitha. The hill is unusual for carrying Hindu, Jain and Buddhist associations together, including a footprint attributed to the Jain tirthankara Parshvanatha and a Jain temple built in 1682, destroyed and later rebuilt.
story: Devotees hold that the womb of Sati fell on this hill, and that the Pandavas, and later Rama with Sita and Lakshmana, sheltered here during their forest exiles.
